failure_modes: Survivorship bias. The universe is screened from today's index membership, so twelve years of survivorship run in the candidate's favour. Direction is named in advance: it inflates momentum more than buy-and-hold, so a PASS here would be suspect while a FAIL is if anything understated.
Benign period. 2014-2019 contains no COVID crash and no 2022 bear market, which flatters any long-only trend rule.
Low trade count. A concentrated top-decile rule places few trades, so the per-trade confidence interval will be wide and an INCONCLUSIVE significance result must not be read as support.
A PASS would still not be permission to enable anything. It would be one period, one parameterisation, and would need the full walk-forward and the live gate before it meant anything.
spec.prior: EDGE claims stand at 0 for 7 entering this test. The honest prior is that this fails too: a rule published thirty-three years ago and widely known has had a third of a century to be arbitraged away. What makes the result worth having is not the probability of passing but that no selection step exists, so the verdict cannot be an artifact of choosing.
spec.title: Pre-specified cross-sectional momentum (Jegadeesh & Titman 1993), no selection

failure_modes: SURVIVORSHIP, and it is severe here — worse than in any previous section. The universe is screened from TODAY'S S&P 1500 membership, so every company that went bankrupt or was delisted in the 2008 crisis is absent by construction. The crash is therefore systematically softened, and long-only momentum benefits most from that. Direction named in advance: this inflates every arm, so a PASS here would be weak evidence while a FAIL is strong.

The screen measures liquidity on the FIRST calendar year only (2007), so universe selection cannot peek at the test window. That is a guard, not a guarantee: 2007 liquidity itself reflects pre-crisis conditions.

Three arms share a snapshot and a universe, so their results are strongly correlated. "All three moved" is therefore much weaker evidence than three independent confirmations, and must not be read as such.
Low trade count. A top-decile rule places few trades, so per-arm confidence intervals will be wide and an INCONCLUSIVE significance result is not support.

A PASS is not permission to enable anything. It would be one family, one period, one universe construction — and it would still owe a walk-forward on a period with no survivorship advantage before it meant anything.
spec.prior: This fails. EDGE claims stand at 0 for 8, and §35 already ran xsmom-12-1 on 2014-2019 where it lost 4.04% while the market gained 90.41%. The reason to run it anyway is that 2007-2013 is the first period this repository has ever scored that contains a real bear market, and §35's registration named "benign period" as a failure mode that has stood unanswered since. A three-arm family requirement also makes a lucky single-arm result impossible to mistake for an effect. If momentum has any regime in which it earns its keep, a crisis is the most-claimed one; if it fails here too, that claim is answered on this repository's own data rather than by assertion.
spec.title: Cross-sectional momentum family coherence, 2007-2013 (incl. the GFC)

failure_modes: PERIOD ALREADY MINED. §32 scored 2020-2026 with these families. This is a subset. Any result is a re-description of spent evidence and must never be cited as confirmation of §37 — two readings of overlapping data are not two independent results.

Survivorship again, though far milder than §37's: the universe is today's index membership screened on 2022 liquidity, so recent delistings are absent. Over four years that matters much less than over the 2008 crisis.
A short window. 2022-2026 is ~4.5 years and contains one bear market (2022) followed by a long recovery, so it is close to a single regime.

The strongest temptation this file must resist: if these arms happen to look good here while failing in §37, that is the textbook shape of a period-specific fluke, and §34 already established this repository cannot tell such a fluke from an effect. It would be a reason to distrust the number, not to enable anything.
spec.prior: No expectation is recorded, because a prior is what makes a test falsifiable and this is not a test. §32 already rejected these families on a period that contains this one, so the answer is substantially known and stating a confident prior would be dressing foreknowledge as prediction. What this actually buys is comparability: identical arms and pass mark against §37, so the difference between a crisis period and a recent one can be read directly. If §37's monotone damage by lookback also appears here, that consistency is worth knowing; if it does not, the instability across regimes is itself the observation, and it is the same instability §34 found when no selector could beat a coin.
spec.title: Momentum family on 2022-2026 — DIAGNOSTIC, decides nothing (§32 already mined this period)

failure_modes: SURVIVORSHIP, severe. The universe is today's S&P 1500 membership screened on 2000 liquidity, so the dot-com casualties are absent by construction — the companies that went to zero between 2000 and 2002 were never fetched. This flatters ANY long strategy including the incumbent, so a FAIL here is strong evidence and a PASS is weak. Same direction as §37, same asymmetry.

The strategies were tuned on 2020-2026 38-symbol data (§14-§29). Running them on a 500-symbol universe from a different era changes two things at once, so a poor result cannot be attributed to the period alone — the breadth of the universe is a confound and is not being controlled here.

Low deployment makes `beats_exposure_matched` easy in a way that is arithmetically correct and substantively hollow: a bot 92% in cash faces a bar of 8% of the market's return. Clause (d) stops the degenerate case, but a marginal PASS at very low deployment should be read as "it barely invested", not as "it has edge".

2000-2006 contains a crash and a full recovery, which is a favourable shape for a long-only rules engine measured on total return. A single period cannot separate skill from having been pointed at a rising 2003-2006.
A PASS would NOT mean the live bot is working. It would mean one configuration cleared one gate on one unseen period, and it would still owe the live 30-trade evidence gate before anything changed.
spec.prior: The incumbent probably fails, and the reason is already written into this file rather than being a hunch. The ALREADY-SEEN OBSERVATION recorded before this registration shows the same test applied to three periods whose numbers were produced as baselines for other claims: 2007-2013 fails (+0.78% against a +9.65% bar), 2022-2026 fails (-11.62% against +3.75%), and 2014-2019 passes by 1.44pp at 70% deployment. Roughly one in three. 2000-2006 has never been scored here, so this is the first honest test of the question, and the honest expectation is failure. What makes it worth running anyway is that nine candidate rejections say less about whether this bot should be trading than one clean answer about the incumbent.
spec.title: Does the live ensemble clear its own enablement gate on 2000-2006?
